# Upbound Group (UPBD): a deep dive on management and the setup
*Five earnings calls, Q3 2025 (2025-10-30) to Q3 2026 (2026-10-29). Price used: $22.84 (NASDAQ, USD, FMP quote 2026-11-02).*

Upbound is the parent of Rent-A-Center (about 1,500+ corporate stores that rent furniture, appliances and electronics on a lease-to-own basis), Acima (the same lease-to-own product embedded at third-party retailers' checkouts and online) and Brigit (a subscription app that offers small cash advances, called earned-wage access, plus credit-building tools). The screener tags it as software. It is not software. It is a lender to subprime consumers, and its economics are driven by the losses it takes on leases. Read it that way.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

**The story shrank from growth to underwriting discipline, and that change worked.**

- **Q3 2025 (2025-10-30):** management said Acima was "on track to deliver high single digits to low double-digit GMV growth" (GMV is gross merchandise volume, the dollar value of new leases written). The same call conceded that some 2025 lease cohorts were going bad. Lease charge-offs rose 50 basis points, the company tightened approvals "each month", and it warned that losses would peak in Q4 2025.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-02-19):** the framing became about getting back to normal. Management guided Acima losses to "that 9.5% range" for 2026 and said the most recent cohorts were "much more in line with historical years".
- **Q1 2026 (2026-04-30):** charge-offs fell to about 8.8%, a 130 basis-point improvement from Q4. GMV came in "below our expectations", lower than a year earlier. Growth was now explicitly second to portfolio health.
- **Q2 2026 (2026-07-30):** management said it was "trading risk-adjusted margin for volume". The loss guide was cut to "around 9%, if not below 9%" and Acima's EBITDA margin passed 16%. The quarter also included a disclosed ~$13M fraud loss at Acima.
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-29):** the story is now about profit and cash. Charge-offs were 8.7%, "the lowest level since stimulus in 2021". Acima GMV was down 11% year over year. Free cash flow was $121M in the quarter and net leverage was 2.4x. The company announced a $50M buyback "this quarter" and created a new chief operating officer role. It also guided Q4 GMV to "relatively flat", which would end three quarters of decline.

The growth drivers the company added along the way have held up: Brigit (paying users up 27% to 1.84M, revenue up 37%), an Experian distribution deal for Brigit, a Boost Mobile point-of-sale integration across about 5,000 stores, and an Amazon pickup partnership adding about 50 visits per store per week at Rent-A-Center. The Acima growth claim of 2025 was quietly dropped.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Losses would peak in Q4 2025 and normalize | Charge-offs went from ~10% (Q4 2025) to 8.8% (Q1), 8.8% (Q2) and 8.7% (Q3 2026) | Delivered |
| Q3 2026 beat guidance | Non-GAAP EPS $1.01 against a $0.85-0.95 guide; adjusted EBITDA $123M against $105-115M; revenue $1.15B at the top of the $1.05-1.15B range | Delivered (beat 7 of 7 quarters per the screener) |
| "Significant free cash flow" | TTM free cash flow $481M; Q3 FCF $121M, more than double the prior year | True, but flattered (see below) |
| Deleveraging toward the 2x target | Net leverage 2.4x; balance-sheet net debt $1.51B including leases, about $1.22B excluding leases | Delivered |
| Profit growth | GAAP diluted EPS: Q3 2026 $0.58 vs $0.22 a year earlier; TTM $1.90 vs FY2025 $1.25 | Real recovery from a weak base |
| Growth | Revenue down 1.6% y/y in Q3 ($1.146B vs $1.165B); Acima GMV down 11% | Revenue is flat to shrinking |

**Two forensic cautions.**
1. **Cash flow is flattered by shrinkage.** The CFO said cash flow was strong "partly due to some of the softness that we've seen on the top line and a reduction of overall working capital." A lease-to-own company buys inventory to lease out, so writing fewer leases releases cash. The $481M TTM free cash flow is not a run-rate. The FY2026 free-cash-flow guide is about $250M, after "substantial legal payments" tied to a multi-state attorney-general investigation. When GMV grows again, the company has to reinvest in inventory, and free cash flow will fall back toward its reported earnings.
2. **Non-GAAP and GAAP earnings are far apart.** Q3 non-GAAP EPS was $1.01 and GAAP was $0.58. The FY2026 non-GAAP guide is $4.00-4.35, while TTM GAAP EPS is $1.90. The gap is mostly amortization of intangibles from the Acima and Brigit acquisitions, which is a real non-cash charge to exclude. But it also removes stock compensation and recurring legal and regulatory charges, which are real costs in this industry. Our estimate of earnings power sits between the two: about $3.50 per share.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rating: Rising, from defensive to confident.**
- Q3 2025: on the back foot, explaining bad cohorts ("softness in recent vintages").
- Q4 2025 and Q1 2026: steadier. "Validates the data-driven approach."
- Q2 2026: confident on credit and frank about volume ("trading risk-adjusted margin for volume").

The loss-rate path was called correctly three quarters ahead. Q3 2026 beat the top of every range. - **Volume:** analysts keep asking when GMV turns. The answer has moved from "growth" (2025) to "flat in Q4" (2026-10-29). This is the open question.

- Green: lease charge-offs at 8.7% in Q3 2026, the best since 2021, after a correctly forecast peak in Q4 2025.
- Green: Acima adjusted EBITDA up 15% in Q3 2026 with margin up ~270 basis points to 14.7%.

- Red: Acima GMV down 11% (Q3 2026), and consolidated revenue is down year over year. The lease book is shrinking.
- Red: an attorney-general investigation with "substantial" payments of undisclosed size (2026-10-29), plus a data-breach claims investigation (2026-10-01).
- Red: a ~$13M fraud loss at Acima in Q2 2026.

- "Underwriting capabilities are our core strength" (Q3 2026) shows the company now presents itself as a credit-risk manager rather than a retailer, which fits the peer set.
- A newly created chief operating officer role "unify[ing] business segments under a single leader" (2026-09-22) points to cost and integration work across the three brands. Overlap between the brands is only 10-15% today.

- The buyback "coming out of blackout" signals that management thinks the stock is cheap at around $20.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STRENGTHENING.** Credit, margins, leverage and cash returns have all improved for three straight quarters, and management has delivered on its guidance.

**The single thing to weigh before sizing:** the stock is cheap on earnings (about 5.4x the FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guide midpoint, a 6.8% dividend yield) and expensive on growth (the lease book is shrinking). Today's free cash flow partly comes from that shrinkage, and it is reduced by an unquantified attorney-general settlement. Underwrite earnings power of about $3.50 per share, not the $481M TTM free cash flow.

**Moat:** narrow. It rests on scale and cost, plus underwriting data built from decades of subprime lease outcomes and an embedded merchant network (Acima at checkout, Boost Mobile, Amazon pickup). Returns are low (ROIC about 4.6%, ROE about 11.6%) but recovering, not falling, so the moat is stable rather than eroding. **Secular threat:** manageable. Upbound is the parent of Rent-A-Center (about 1,500+ corporate stores that rent furniture, appliances and electronics on a lease-to-own basis), Acima (the same lease-to-own product embedded at third-party retailers' checkouts and online) and Brigit (a subscription app that offers small cash advances, called earned-wage access, plus credit-building tools). The screener tags it as software. It is not software. It is a lender to subprime consumers, and its economics are driven by the losses it takes on leases. Read it that way.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

**The story shrank from growth to underwriting discipline, and that change worked.**

- **Q3 2025 (2025-10-30):** management said Acima was "on track to deliver high single digits to low double-digit GMV growth" (GMV is gross merchandise volume, the dollar value of new leases written). The same call conceded that some 2025 lease cohorts were going bad. Lease charge-offs rose 50 basis points, the company tightened approvals "each month", and it warned that losses would peak in Q4 2025.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-02-19):** the framing became about getting back to normal. Management guided Acima losses to "that 9.5% range" for 2026 and said the most recent cohorts were "much more in line with historical years".
- **Q1 2026 (2026-04-30):** charge-offs fell to about 8.8%, a 130 basis-point improvement from Q4. GMV came in "below our expectations", lower than a year earlier. Growth was now explicitly second to portfolio health.
- **Q2 2026 (2026-07-30):** management said it was "trading risk-adjusted margin for volume". The loss guide was cut to "around 9%, if not below 9%" and Acima's EBITDA margin passed 16%. The quarter also included a disclosed ~$13M fraud loss at Acima.
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-29):** the story is now about profit and cash. Charge-offs were 8.7%, "the lowest level since stimulus in 2021". Acima GMV was down 11% year over year. Free cash flow was $121M in the quarter and net leverage was 2.4x. The company announced a $50M buyback "this quarter" and created a new chief operating officer role. It also guided Q4 GMV to "relatively flat", which would end three quarters of decline.

The growth drivers the company added along the way have held up: Brigit (paying users up 27% to 1.84M, revenue up 37%), an Experian distribution deal for Brigit, a Boost Mobile point-of-sale integration across about 5,000 stores, and an Amazon pickup partnership adding about 50 visits per store per week at Rent-A-Center. The Acima growth claim of 2025 was quietly dropped.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Losses would peak in Q4 2025 and normalize | Charge-offs went from ~10% (Q4 2025) to 8.8% (Q1), 8.8% (Q2) and 8.7% (Q3 2026) | Delivered |
| Q3 2026 beat guidance | Non-GAAP EPS $1.01 against a $0.85-0.95 guide; adjusted EBITDA $123M against $105-115M; revenue $1.15B at the top of the $1.05-1.15B range | Delivered (beat 7 of 7 quarters per the screener) |
| "Significant free cash flow" | TTM free cash flow $481M; Q3 FCF $121M, more than double the prior year | True, but flattered (see below) |
| Deleveraging toward the 2x target | Net leverage 2.4x; balance-sheet net debt $1.51B including leases, about $1.22B excluding leases | Delivered |
| Profit growth | GAAP diluted EPS: Q3 2026 $0.58 vs $0.22 a year earlier; TTM $1.90 vs FY2025 $1.25 | Real recovery from a weak base |
| Growth | Revenue down 1.6% y/y in Q3 ($1.146B vs $1.165B); Acima GMV down 11% | Revenue is flat to shrinking |

**Two forensic cautions.**
1. **Cash flow is flattered by shrinkage.** The CFO said cash flow was strong "partly due to some of the softness that we've seen on the top line and a reduction of overall working capital." A lease-to-own company buys inventory to lease out, so writing fewer leases releases cash. The $481M TTM free cash flow is not a run-rate. The FY2026 free-cash-flow guide is about $250M, after "substantial legal payments" tied to a multi-state attorney-general investigation. When GMV grows again, the company has to reinvest in inventory, and free cash flow will fall back toward its reported earnings.
2. **Non-GAAP and GAAP earnings are far apart.** Q3 non-GAAP EPS was $1.01 and GAAP was $0.58. The FY2026 non-GAAP guide is $4.00-4.35, while TTM GAAP EPS is $1.90. The gap is mostly amortization of intangibles from the Acima and Brigit acquisitions, which is a real non-cash charge to exclude. But it also removes stock compensation and recurring legal and regulatory charges, which are real costs in this industry. Our estimate of earnings power sits between the two: about $3.50 per share.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rating: Rising, from defensive to confident.**
- Q3 2025: on the back foot, explaining bad cohorts ("softness in recent vintages").
- Q4 2025 and Q1 2026: steadier. "Validates the data-driven approach."
- Q2 2026: confident on credit and frank about volume ("trading risk-adjusted margin for volume").
- Q3 2026: offensive again. "Bullish on the holiday season", a buyback, new hires in leadership, and "flexibility to adjust that lever" (loosening underwriting). It is still careful about the consumer: "cautious around where the consumer is going to spend."

Guidance has become more specific over time, with quarterly ranges and named loss-rate targets. That is a good sign.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

The loss-rate path was called correctly three quarters ahead. Q3 2026 beat the top of every range. Full-year non-GAAP EPS of $4.00-4.35 was reaffirmed on 2026-07-30, and the free-cash-flow guide was raised to about $250M. The one large miss was the Acima volume promise from 2025 (high single to low double-digit growth), which turned into an 11% decline. That miss was a choice made for credit reasons, not a forecasting failure. The guidance ranges have been wide enough to beat, which looks like mild sandbagging (setting targets low enough to clear). **Reliability: High on profit and credit, Medium on volume.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Volume:** analysts keep asking when GMV turns. The answer has moved from "growth" (2025) to "flat in Q4" (2026-10-29). This is the open question.
- **Cash conversion:** Bank of America asked on 2026-10-29 about the gap between $400M of operating cash flow and $250M of free cash flow. The answer was the attorney-general legal payments, and no amount was given. The size of that settlement is a real, unquantified liability.
- **Capital allocation after Brigit:** management said it is "not being proactive at this point around M&A", which is reassuring.
- **What analysts are not pushing on:** regulation of earned-wage access at Brigit, and the 2026-10-01 data-breach class-action investigation (Ademi LLP). Neither came up on the call.
- **Coverage is thin:** one price target in the last year ($28, 2026-07-31).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Green: lease charge-offs at 8.7% in Q3 2026, the best since 2021, after a correctly forecast peak in Q4 2025.
- Green: Acima adjusted EBITDA up 15% in Q3 2026 with margin up ~270 basis points to 14.7%.
- Green: Brigit revenue up 37% and EBITDA up 59% in Q3 2026. This is the growth asset.
- Green: net leverage 2.4x heading to 2x. A $50M buyback (about 4% of market cap) was announced 2026-10-29. The $0.39 quarterly dividend was maintained (declared 2026-09-24). Insiders made 8 open-market buys against 1 sale.
- Red: Acima GMV down 11% (Q3 2026), and consolidated revenue is down year over year. The lease book is shrinking.
- Red: an attorney-general investigation with "substantial" payments of undisclosed size (2026-10-29), plus a data-breach claims investigation (2026-10-01).
- Red: a ~$13M fraud loss at Acima in Q2 2026.
- Red: the core customer is squeezed by groceries, rent, utilities and gas (CEO, 2026-10-29). Gross margin has fallen from 61.6% (2019) to about 48-51% today, partly because Acima's business mix carries lower margins.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "Underwriting capabilities are our core strength" (Q3 2026) shows the company now presents itself as a credit-risk manager rather than a retailer, which fits the peer set.
- A newly created chief operating officer role "unify[ing] business segments under a single leader" (2026-09-22) points to cost and integration work across the three brands. Overlap between the brands is only 10-15% today.
- AI comes up more often (about half of code changes "involve AI assistance"). This is efficiency talk, not a revenue claim.
- The buyback "coming out of blackout" signals that management thinks the stock is cheap at around $20.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STRENGTHENING.** Credit, margins, leverage and cash returns have all improved for three straight quarters, and management has delivered on its guidance.

**The single thing to weigh before sizing:** the stock is cheap on earnings (about 5.4x the FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guide midpoint, a 6.8% dividend yield) and expensive on growth (the lease book is shrinking). Today's free cash flow partly comes from that shrinkage, and it is reduced by an unquantified attorney-general settlement. Underwrite earnings power of about $3.50 per share, not the $481M TTM free cash flow.

**Moat:** narrow. It rests on scale and cost, plus underwriting data built from decades of subprime lease outcomes and an embedded merchant network (Acima at checkout, Boost Mobile, Amazon pickup). Returns are low (ROIC about 4.6%, ROE about 11.6%) but recovering, not falling, so the moat is stable rather than eroding. **Secular threat:** manageable. Buy-now-pay-later lenders and the shift of retail to e-commerce pressure the store-based Rent-A-Center, but Acima already sits on the e-commerce and virtual channel and Rent-A-Center same-store sales have grown for four quarters. The cheapness looks like a cyclical fear of subprime credit plus a regulatory overhang, not a structurally shrinking base. The risk is consumer-cycle risk, not terminal risk.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

Full-year non-GAAP EPS of $4.00-4.35 was reaffirmed on 2026-07-30, and the free-cash-flow guide was raised to about $250M. The one large miss was the Acima volume promise from 2025 (high single to low double-digit growth), which turned into an 11% decline. That miss was a choice made for credit reasons, not a forecasting failure. The guidance ranges have been wide enough to beat, which looks like mild sandbagging (setting targets low enough to clear). **Reliability: High on profit and credit, Medium on volume.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Volume:** analysts keep asking when GMV turns. The answer has moved from "growth" (2025) to "flat in Q4" (2026-10-29). This is the open question.

- Green: lease charge-offs at 8.7% in Q3 2026, the best since 2021, after a correctly forecast peak in Q4 2025.
- Green: Acima adjusted EBITDA up 15% in Q3 2026 with margin up ~270 basis points to 14.7%.

- Red: Acima GMV down 11% (Q3 2026), and consolidated revenue is down year over year. The lease book is shrinking.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "Underwriting capabilities are our core strength" (Q3 2026) shows the company now presents itself as a credit-risk manager rather than a retailer, which fits the peer set.
- A newly created chief operating officer role "unify[ing] business segments under a single leader" (2026-09-22) points to cost and integration work across the three brands. Overlap between the brands is only 10-15% today.
- AI comes up more often (about half of code changes "involve AI assistance"). This is efficiency talk, not a revenue claim.
- The buyback "coming out of blackout" signals that management thinks the stock is cheap at around $20.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STRENGTHENING.** Credit, margins, leverage and cash returns have all improved for three straight quarters, and management has delivered on its guidance.

**The single thing to weigh before sizing:** the stock is cheap on earnings (about 5.4x the FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guide midpoint, a 6.8% dividend yield) and expensive on growth (the lease book is shrinking). Today's free cash flow partly comes from that shrinkage, and it is reduced by an unquantified attorney-general settlement. Underwrite earnings power of about $3.50 per share, not the $481M TTM free cash flow.

**Moat:** narrow. It rests on scale and cost, plus underwriting data built from decades of subprime lease outcomes and an embedded merchant network (Acima at checkout, Boost Mobile, Amazon pickup). Returns are low (ROIC about 4.6%, ROE about 11.6%) but recovering, not falling, so the moat is stable rather than eroding. **Secular threat:** manageable. Buy-now-pay-later lenders and the shift of retail to e-commerce pressure the store-based Rent-A-Center, but Acima already sits on the e-commerce and virtual channel and Rent-A-Center same-store sales have grown for four quarters. The cheapness looks like a cyclical fear of subprime credit plus a regulatory overhang, not a structurally shrinking base. The risk is consumer-cycle risk, not terminal risk.
